title: Solo developer looking for feedback on my Football Manager game
author: Erdal3666
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I've been developing Global Football Manager in Godot as a solo developer.

The game isn't released yet, and this isn't a promotion. I'm sharing an early gameplay video because I'd love to get honest feedback from fellow Godot developers.

I'm especially interested in your thoughts on:

2D match engine

UI/UX

Animations

Overall game feel

Any criticism or suggestions are greatly appreciated. Thanks!

comments.author: count023
comments.body: you should b careful using the name football manager, i think you'll find that's trademarked by EA.

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body: Thanks for the warning! I'll definitely look into the trademark situation. If necessary, I'll change the branding before release. I appreciate you pointing it out.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
for me to be motivated long term i would need so see some faces. like player faces, whatever generated but i need to identify and become attached to certain players and that is extremely hard when they are only ever a name and a number. i dont know if a generator or a collection of billions of portraits would be better (probably the later) but i personally would NEED everyone to have a picture and then show this picture for example also at the bottom in simulation with a bit of a "announcer" style text currating the game "oh he did shoot but missed by a mile. well, better luck next time" ... stuff like that. 

currently it looks like you never ever put player appeal in your eyes and only mechanic

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body: Thank you, this is really valuable feedback. You're right that emotional attachment to players is important in a football manager game. I'm currently focusing on building the core mechanics first, but player portraits, match event visuals, and more personality are all planned. My goal is to make every generated player feel unique, not just a name and a number. Thanks for taking the time to explain your thoughts!

comments.author: starrftw
comments.body:
Hey, I’m into FM games and alternatives since Championship Manager 2006. 
What’s your plan for first playable version? Feels like it’s most challenging part — core loop usually kicks in when all key system finally start working together. Like, if transfer system doesn’t work properly — whole immersion vibe goes down drastically. 
You already have great barebones for improvements. Extra question: what’s the rest of your tech stack and especially agent harness.

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body:
Thanks! I really appreciate the thoughtful feedback.
My goal for the first playable version is to have the full core loop working: scouting, transfers, squad management, tactics, match simulation, finances, and progression through multiple seasons. I agree that if the transfer market doesn't feel believable, the whole manager experience suffers.
Right now I'm focusing on making each system work together before adding more content and polish.
As for the tech stack, the game is being built in Godot 4 with GDScript. I'm also using OpenAI Codex as an AI coding assistant to speed up development, prototyping, and refactoring, while all design decisions and gameplay systems are implemented and iterated by me.
My long-term goal is to create a manager game that feels dynamic and replayable rather than just a database simulator.

comments.author: BitsOnWaves
comments.body: try working on changing the obvoius generic AI UI desgin ... people are getting sick of it

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback! I actually agree.

The current UI is just a placeholder while I focus on the core gameplay and match engine. A complete visual redesign with a more unique identity is planned before release.

I'd rather get the gameplay right first, then polish the presentation.

comments.author: BritishDystopia
comments.body: What's the deal with that strange long, narrow pitch. Immediate hard pass for me with that.

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body: Thanks for the honest feedback! The current pitch is just a temporary placeholder while I'm building the core match engine. A more realistic pitch with improved camera angles and visuals is already planned before release.

comments.author: HomeTimeLegend
comments.body: What's the purpose of this, like hows it different than FM? It seems like you're going for an almost completely copy which is a ton of work for you especially if there's no reason for anyone to ever play it over FM.

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body:
Default

Thanks! That's a fair point.

I'm not trying to replace Football Manager. FM is an amazing game.

My goal is to build a free, mobile-first football management game that's easy to pick up but still deep enough for long-term play. FM is a premium PC experience, while I'm focusing on quick sessions, accessibility, and continuous community-driven updates.

The first versions will naturally look similar because football management games share many core mechanics. Over time, I want to add features that make the game stand on its own.

I really appreciate the feedback—comments like this help shape the direction of the project.

replies.author: HomeTimeLegend
replies.body: Great, you've clearly put a lot of work in. I worry you'll have too much competition, most of them will be poor games but getting seen could be a problem... Worst case scenario I imagine you will/have learned a lot and could apply it to all kinds of management/sim games. Good luck!

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: Some of those fonts are so small i would never be able to read them..

replies.author: Erdal3666
replies.body:
Thanks for pointing that out! You're absolutely right.

The UI is still a work in progress, and improving readability is one of my priorities. I'll increase the font sizes and make the interface easier to read, especially on mobile devices.

I appreciate the feedback!
